segments.he: ופ"א אמר מהרנ"ת ז"ל את הכל אני יכול לתאר לי רק את הלילה הראשונה בקבר את זה איני יכול לתאר לי (אלדינג קען איך מיר אוס מאלין נאור דוא ערשטי נאכט אין קבר ניט בעם ערשטין ברוך הבא).
segments.en: After Rabbainu's passing, once Moharan'as encountered Reb Chaykel and told him what Rabbainu had said to him. And he depicted — something that was for Reb Chaykel a great humiliation — how he would have had to go with a big lantern from householder to householder in the town, singing a melody to each one in order to receive Chanukah money from them. "Viya er volt badarft gayn mit dem groisn lastern tsi yedn bazunder un zingen im a nigun — kedey tsi nemen bay im Chanukah gelt." And Moharan'as rebuked him: "I thought at least you regret this — but you still do not regret it and still cling to your cleverness." Once Reb Chaykel had a legal dispute with a woman who disgraced him, calling him "Chaykel shagets" [Chaykel the rascal]. He was astonished and said: "This I did not imagine. I thought if I had been with Rabbainu they would call me Reb Chaykel — and now they call me Chaykel. But that they would call me Chaykel shagets — this I did not think possible." Once he was in Berdichev and Reb Mordechai of Chernobyl encountered them there. All presented their petitions and requests to him. Reb Chaykel stood silently. Reb Mordechai said: "Reb Chaykel — why are you silent? What is your request?" Reb Chaykel replied in a deep voice: "Tzaros levavi hirchivu — mimetzukosai hotzieni" [The troubles of my heart are many — from my anguish bring me out]. Reb Mordechai of Chernobyl was deeply moved and said: "See the difference between them and a Breslov Chassid — for each of them requests their own thing: this one requests livelihood, that one that his business goes well, and not one of them asks about the troubles of the soul. But a Breslov Chassid cries out primarily about the troubles of the soul."
